newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Profit-taking pulls Budapest bourse index down.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pulls Budapest bourse index down.

text.p: Hungarian share prices finished mixed on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, pulling the BUX index a little lower, traders said.
They explained the market's fall by continuing profit-taking but saw the current decline bottoming out soon.
The BUX index closed the fourth successive losing session at 3,604.99 points, down 10.76 from Tuesday. On Wednesday the BSE was closed due to a public holiday.
"The correction continued as the market was overvalued but I think this (correction) is only temporary," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft.
"Sooner or later the market will recoup but now investors are locking in profits," he said, adding he saw the market's floor at around 3,500 to 3,550 points.
The trader mentioned credit rating agencies Moody's and S&P widely expected upgrading of the country's ratings as one reason for optimism.
"If Hungary's rating is modified, new doors may open ahead us," he said.

Traders also expected share prices to benefit from the country's most recent macroeconomic figures, such as current account and trade deficits, reserves and foreign debt, released by the central bank on Tuesday.

"The figures are basically good as the current account deficit narrowed, the net debt fell and reserves grew," Stalmayer said. He added that third-quarter corporate results will also have a positive impact.
Oil company MOL was among the losers on Thursday, dropping 40 forints to end at 1,600.
Pharmaceuticals company Horizon-Multiplan fell two forints to close at 248 forints, after Creditanstalt Securities rated it as "sell" on Tuesday.
